title: Murchunga (Nepali jaw harp)
summary: The murchunga is a small iron jaw harp from the hills of Nepal. The player rests the frame lightly on the teeth and plucks a thin steel tongue that hums one low note. Opening and shaping the mouth then lifts higher overtones out of that hum, so a whole melody comes from a single vibrating strip.
howToPlay: Eight lanes climb like a ladder of overtones: low at the bottom, high at the top.
Watch a bead rise from the tongue towards its lane.
Strike the lane just as the bead arrives.
Begin with the hill dance, then try the staircase of overtones.
rules: The lanes are the fourth to the twelfth overtones of one low tongue note.
A stroke on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and extra strokes lose points.
Every song is played through twice.
Neighbouring lanes are a small change of the mouth; far lanes need a bigger change.
Every sound is the same plucked tongue; only the mouth shape changes the pitch you hear.
heritageNote: Jaw harps have been forged and played across Asia for many centuries. In Nepal's hills the murchunga accompanies dance and song, and players often use it to murmur tunes between friends.
